question: With router.cleanup.remove_stubs=true and the stub test counting contacts as KiCad does (any same-net copper overlap on a shared layer, Q16.4), does a plugin run with the plugin45 options leave no dangling via or track visible from the DSN on canary-pwr and four KiCad demos Q16.3 did not use, without raising any board's KiCad-unconnected count, adding a DRC error, or losing determinism?
rule_text: N02 (docs/roadmap/tasks/N02-keep-rule-for-defaults.md) with accept no-regress, as Q16.json: the candidate passes against the baseline arm when the KiCad-unconnected total over the distinct boards is not worse than the set's noise (sqrt of the sum of the per-board bands squared). Hard guards, each on every board: kicad_unconnected of the candidate not above the baseline's (a rise of 1 fails, whatever the noise), drc_real not above the baseline's, via_in_pad = 0, below_minimum = 0, via_dangling_dsn = 0 and track_dangling_dsn = 0 in the candidate; determinism (D2): the candidate's CLI run on each board is run twice and the two SES files are byte-identical. via_dangling_dsn and track_dangling_dsn are KiCad's via_dangling and track_dangling minus the findings tools/kicad-oracle/dangling_visible.py classifies as the plane-fill limit (the via centre or a track end inside a DSN plane polygon of its net on that layer and outside KiCad's fill of the net there: the router sees a plane contact the DSN shows and KiCad's fill does not, which no stage can know; the operator's decision of 2026-10-18). A board whose baseline has no dangling copper still counts in the totals and the guards. pass_rule below is the parser's paired rule, kept only so the file validates; it does not decide.

noise.formula: max(2, 0.05 * the unconnected count of the unrouted input board, by KiCad's DRC), given to the gate as each row's connections

plugin45.engine: freerouting-rs release CLI at origin/main 27d7409 plus Q16.4's diff (the stub test on overlap contacts; nothing else of the engine changes), profile enhanced as it is there (power_layer_traces=none, neck_width_um=300), through kicad-plugin/headless_run.py (the plugin's export, fix-ups, arguments and ImportSpecctraSES), WSL KiCad 10.0.7
plugin45.what: baseline: the plugin45 options under the current enhanced, the cleanup unset

plugin45+cleanup.what: candidate: plugin45 plus Q16's final stub cleanup with Q16.4's contacts

boards.procedure: canary-pwr as Q16.json (the git archive of canary HEAD e21ee05e hardware/canary-pwr-rev1.0, the plugin path, --schematic-parity). The demos are KiCad 10.0.7's /usr/share/kicad/demos with tracks and vias stripped by tools/kicad-oracle/kicad_steps.py strip (hashes of the stripped boards; the strip is reproducible, StickHub stripped twice gave the same bytes), each with its own .kicad_pro: kit-dev-coldfire-xilinx_5213 (4 copper layers; K02.7's graded Rust run had 48 via_dangling), StickHub (2 layers), RoyalBlue54L-Feather (8 layers) and multichannel_mixer (2 layers, from multichannel_mixer-unrouted.kicad_pcb with multichannel_mixer.kicad_pro). Chosen before any number of this registration: the multi-layer demos with vias that Q16.1 and Q16.3 did not use, of a size that routes in minutes; ecc83-pp and complex_hierarchy are left out because K02.7's runs had no dangling copper on them, jetson-agx-thor-baseboard, vme-wren and video for their size. Only kit-dev-coldfire-xilinx_5213 is known to have dangling vias in a baseline (K02.7, other options); the others have no prior grade.

grading: kicad-cli pcb drc --refill-zones --save-board --severity-all --format json on the board ImportSpecctraSES saved (canary-pwr also --schematic-parity, inside the canary HEAD project copy); canary's via_in_pad.py (WSL KiCad python); tools/kicad-oracle/dangling_visible.py on the saved board, that DRC report and the DSN of the run. drc_real = error-severity violations other than unconnected_items and starved_thermal, minus the same types on the unrouted input (its own DRC with the same flags); below_minimum = the track_width errors
keep_rule: if the candidate passes, N05 adds cleanup.remove_stubs = true to ENHANCED with these numbers (profile.rs entry, the settings_profile test, the DIVERGENCES line, the help text, an N05.3 line); if it fails, the setting stays unset in both profiles and Q16.4's note gives the numbers and the cause of each failing guard
stop_rule: one registered run per arm per board, plus the candidate's determinism rerun; no reruns with other settings
